sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Acute Stabilization of Anaphylaxis
sections.description: This section establishes the foundational recognition of anaphylaxis using the case presentation, detailing the classic signs, symptoms, and immediate life-saving interventions required in the Emergency Department.
subtopics: Defining anaphylaxis: Criteria involving airway, breathing, circulation, and cutaneous manifestations
Case analysis: Identifying the trigger (clarithromycin) and timeline of symptom onset
Initial assessment: Recognizing hypotension, hypoxia, and generalized urticaria
First-line management: The critical role of intramuscular epinephrine
Adjunctive therapies: Fluid resuscitation, oxygen supplementation, and antihistamines
Addressing dosing discrepancies: The impact of 0.3 mg vs. 0.5 mg epinephrine auto-injectors in adult patients

sections.section_title: Navigating Complex Courses: Biphasic and Multiphasic Anaphylaxis
sections.description: This section differentiates between simple resolution, biphasic reactions, and the rare multiphasic presentation seen in this case, focusing on the clinical challenges of recurring symptoms despite initial stabilization.
subtopics: Definitions: Distinguishing biphasic, multiphasic, refractory, and protracted anaphylaxis
Pathophysiology of recurrence: Why symptoms return without re-exposure to the allergen
Epidemiology and risk factors: Incidence rates and predictors of biphasic/multiphasic events
Case progression: Analyzing the four distinct episodes of shock in the patient
The waning severity phenomenon: Observing decreasing symptom intensity with each relapse
Diagnostic pitfalls: Differentiating true relapse from incomplete initial treatment or ongoing absorption

sections.section_title: Advanced Management Strategies and Therapeutic Controversies
sections.description: This section evaluates the decision-making process for managing recurrent anaphylaxis in the ICU setting, critically appraising the use of corticosteroids and advanced epinephrine delivery methods.
subtopics: Monitoring protocols: Determining appropriate observation durations and ICU transfer criteria
The corticosteroid debate: Reviewing evidence against routine use for preventing biphasic reactions
Advanced intervention options: Continuous IV epinephrine infusion versus expectant management
Decision analysis in the case study: Weighing risks of aggressive pre-emptive treatment vs. reactive care
Supportive care evolution: Adjusting fluid and oxygen needs across multiple episodes
Guideline gaps: Managing scenarios where standard algorithms fail to address multiphasic complexity

sections.section_title: Unmasking Underlying Pathology: The Role of Systemic Mastocytosis
sections.description: This section explores the diagnostic workup triggered by an atypical clinical course, linking severe/recurrent anaphylaxis to underlying mast cell disorders like systemic mastocytosis.
subtopics: When to suspect a mast cell disorder: Red flags in anaphylaxis history and presentation
Diagnostic biomarkers: Proper timing and interpretation of serum tryptase levels (acute vs. baseline)
WHO Diagnostic Criteria for Systemic Mastocytosis: Major and minor criteria application
Case-specific findings: Interpreting elevated baseline tryptase, hepatomegaly, and bone marrow limitations
Associated comorbidities: Neuropsychiatric symptoms and other organ involvement in mastocytosis
